name: CTCMath
line: CTCMath teaches by video, lesson by lesson. AMP chooses the next problem and brings review back.
description: CTCMath teaches K–12 math with short video lessons, then questions. AMP chooses every next problem, mixes in review and prints workbooks for each learner.
verdict: CTCMath is built around short narrated video lessons, each followed by its own questions [1]. AMP starts from the problem: it chooses each next one, explains it there, and brings earlier skills back for review.
theirs: CTCMath gives a homeschool day a clear shape: watch a short tutorial, answer interactive questions or use a worksheet, then look at the results [1].
A membership covers kindergarten through grade 12 and lets a learner move between grades, so a family can go back to earlier material [1][2].
credit: A teacher’s spoken explanation before the learner tries a topic [1].
Automated marking and diagnostic tests by topic [1].
Printable worksheets, one-page lesson summaries and worked solutions [2].
Access to every grade, so earlier lessons stay open [2].

reasons.title: AMP decides what to practice next
reasons.body: CTCMath follows each video with that lesson’s questions [1]. AMP chooses every next problem from what the learner just did, so nobody has to pick the day’s topic.

reasons.title: Review comes back on its own
reasons.body: A child can explain a lesson right after watching it. AMP brings the same skill back days and weeks later, mixed in with other topics.

reasons.title: Gaps get repaired
reasons.body: When a skill keeps going wrong, AMP sends practice back to what that skill builds on, and keeps what is already learned in review.

reasons.title: The explanation is at the problem
reasons.body: Every AMP problem carries a hint, a short lesson and a step-by-step explanation, so help arrives while the learner is working on it.

theirs: CTCMath describes how its lessons work on its own site [1][2]. This comparison makes no claim about studies of CTCMath.
ours: AMP’s research report sets out each part of the program and the published research behind it. It is AMP’s ESSA Tier 4 rationale, and the studies it plans are pre-registered and published whatever the result.

rows.range: Kindergarten through grade 12, with access to every grade [1][2].
rows.next: Each video lesson is followed by its own questions [1].
rows.print: Printable worksheets, one-page lesson summaries and worked solutions [2].
rows.reports: Automated marking, with results to review [1].

them: Your child wants a teacher’s spoken explanation before trying a topic.
You like choosing the lesson and following a watch-then-practice routine.
amp: You want the program to choose what to practice next.
You want review that returns on its own, mixed across topics.
You want printed workbooks made from where each learner is.

questions.question: Does CTCMath include worksheets?
questions.answer: Yes. CTCMath describes printable worksheets, one-page tutorial summaries and worked solutions [2]. AMP prints workbooks made for each learner, with solutions.

questions.question: When is AMP the stronger fit?
questions.answer: When you want the program to choose a continuing mix of practice and review, with an explanation at the problem and printable work for time away from the screen.
